title: Canonical constant-sheaf comparison under scheme inverse image
statement: Let $T$ be any scheme in universe $u$, and let $p_T^*$ be inverse image from the profinite point [sk-def-sfb-pullback-from-point], with abelian coefficients in universe $u+1$. Write $c_*$ and $c_T$ for the constant abelian-sheaf functors on profinite sets and the small pro-etale site of $T$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Define the canonical natural isomorphism $\kappa_T:c_T\xrightarrow{\sim}c_*\circ p_T^*$ by the following adjunction construction. For a continuous site functor $F:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ and a terminal object $V$ of $\mathcal C$ whose image is terminal, precomposition followed by evaluation at $V$ equals evaluation at $F(V)$. Use the sheaf-section/evaluation comparisons to obtain the pushforward-sections natural isomorphism. Conjugate it under the constant-sheaf/terminal-sections adjunctions and the inverse-image adjunction to define the constant-sheaf pullback isomorphism. First apply this construction to profinite sets mapping to the pro-etale site of $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb Z$, obtaining $\kappa_{\mathbb Z}$. Next apply it to base change along $T\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb Z$, using the identity object of that pro-etale site as terminal and its pullback as terminal. Compose this second comparison, the inverse image of $\kappa_{\mathbb Z}$, and the functor associator. This composite is $\kappa_T$. The terminal object is the identity scheme over itself, accessed through the equality specifying that object. The construction requires no finite coefficient ring, nonzero coefficient or nonempty scheme.
